title: Enterprise Prospect Sales Kit — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Ava Chen
summary: A consolidated enterprise prospect sales kit for Redwood Inference covering positioning and messaging, concise competitive briefs, a recommended pitch deck structure, pricing guidance for enterprise deals, two customer case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects. Use this kit to prepare enterprise demos, RFP responses, and security conversations.
audience: Field sales, solutions engineers, sales engineers, account executives, pre-sales leadership
objective: Provide a single, actionable reference that standardizes Redwood’s enterprise positioning, competitive talking points, pricing guardrails, exemplar pitch deck, and security FAQ to reduce cycle time and improve win rates on enterprise deals.
positioning_and_messaging:
Overview:
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that prioritizes predictable economics, low latency, and operational controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. For enterprise prospects, frame Redwood as: 
- A production-grade inference runtime: optimized serving, autoscaling, and smart routing ensure predictable latency and throughput.
- Cost and performance controls: batching, caching, and quantization guidance reduce unit cost without regressions in quality.
- Unified experience across environments: same API, model catalog, and observability whether hosted, dedicated, or private.
- Enterprise controls and SLAs: dedicated capacity and private deployments with KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and compliance support.

Key value props (elevator lines):
- For Product/ML Engineering: "Ship LLM features faster with predictable latency and lower unit costs—use the same API across hosted and private deployments."
- For Platform/SRE: "Centralize inference with observable performance and clear routing policies so apps get consistent SLAs across regions and capacity tiers."
- For Security/Compliance: "Private control plane and on-prem options with encryption and audit trails to meet regulatory requirements."

Proof points to include in conversations:
- Latency SLOs: typical p95 generation latency targets of 150–400ms for conversational workloads on Dedicated (depends on model class and sequence length; reference: model-performance-catalog).
- Cost reductions: 20–55% token-cost savings reported after enabling prefix caching + optimized batching on benchmarking workloads.
- Deployment modes: successfully delivered >25 Private deployments for regulated customers (finance/healthcare) in 2024–2026.

Messaging dos and don’ts:
- Do emphasize unified API and predictable economics; prospects care about operational predictability more than raw model novelty.
- Don’t overpromise latency for unbenchmarked custom models; use the model catalog to set expectations.

Objection handling snippets:
- "We host everything in our VPC; can Redwood work there?" — Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem deployments; we integrate with customer KMS and provide an optional air-gapped package with documented day-2 ops.
- "We’re concerned about cost" — We offer Dedicated reserved capacity with predictable throughput and options for autoscaling and burst capacity. We also provide Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization) and a cost forecast during PoC.
competitive_briefs:
Competitive landscape summary (one-paragraph briefs):
- Large cloud AI platforms (CloudX AI Endpoints): Strengths: integrated infra, global scale, enterprise contracts. Weaknesses: generic runtimes, less inference-specialized optimizations and higher per-token cost for LLM-focused workloads. Positioning: Redwood offers inference-optimized runtime and cost controls focused on production LLM economics.
- LLM API providers (LLMFast / AnswerCloud): Strengths: simple API and rapid model updates. Weaknesses: limited private deployment options and fewer enterprise observability tools. Positioning: Redwood matches API simplicity but adds Dedicated/Private deployment, SLOs, and rich tracing.
- Self-hosted inference vendors (OpenServe / InferenceOps): Strengths: full control and on-prem possibility. Weaknesses: heavy ops burden and long integration cycles. Positioning: Redwood provides the same control with a managed control plane and validated on-prem packaging plus implementation support.

Quick competitive rebuttals (soundbites):
- "We can run cheaper with self-hosting." — Possibly for very high volume and with significant infra investment; Redwood reduces time-to-production, provides continuous runtime optimizations, and includes operational tools that lower total cost of ownership.
- "Cloud provider is already our standard." — Redwood integrates with cloud accounts and networking; we focus on inference optimizations that most cloud endpoints do not provide out-of-the-box.

Feature matrix (talking bullets to use in slides):
- Model catalog & verified profiles: Redwood provides curated open models with verified performance numbers (latency/cost per model).
- Routing & fallbacks: traffic policies by latency/cost/region with automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Observability: per-route token-level cost, latency breakdowns, trace hooks, and error analysis dashboards.
- Security: KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, RBAC and VPC/private control plane.

Competitive battle cards (recommendation): create a 1-page battle card per competitor that includes: one-line positioning, top 3 strengths, top 3 weaknesses, ideal customer profile for competitor, top rebuttals, and an exemplar customer story.
pitch_deck_outline:
Recommended pitch deck (12–16 slides) with speaker notes:
1) Title & One-liner — Customer logo + quick hook: "Token-cost and latency you can predict — everywhere you deploy."
2) Agenda — What we’ll cover and timeboxed demo/Q&A.
3) Customer challenges — Typical pain: inconsistent latency, high unit cost, ops overhead. Use prospect-specific data if available.
4) Redwood at a glance — Product modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), one-line differentiator.
5) How it works (high level) — Serving runtime, smart routing, caching & batching, deployment abstraction. Simple diagram.
6) Developer experience — API examples, SDKs, quickstarts, and per-route observability.
7) Performance & cost proof points — p95 latency targets, unit-cost savings, and benchmarking summary for comparable workloads. Include a small table of model vs p95 vs cost-per-1k-tokens.
8) Deployment options & enterprise controls — Dedicated SLAs, Private VPC/on-prem, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
9) Security & compliance — Certifications, data residency, support model. Speaker note: hand to security reviewer for deep dive.
10) Pricing model & estimate approach — how we price Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and an example TCO calculation.
11) Case studies — 1–2 short customer stories with metrics (throughput, cost impact, time-to-production).
12) PoC proposal & success criteria — suggested timeline, milestones, and evaluation metrics (latency, cost per request, error rate).
13) Commercials & next steps — contracting path, pilot credits, and contacts.
14) Appendix — deeper technical references (architecture, SLOs, runbooks).

Speaker tips: tailor slides 7 and 11 with prospect-specific benchmarking and use the appendix for SRE/security deep dives. Provide an engineer to co-present the performance slide when possible.
pricing_guidance:
Pricing models overview (summary):
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token generation & embedding unit), free-tier + volume discounts, recommended for trials and low-to-medium volumes.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU-backed pools with fixed monthly commit; pricing tiers by GPU family and slot count. Includes autoscaling buffer and optional burst capacity. Recommended for predictable throughput and performance-sensitive applications.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): platform fee + deployment/enablement fee + optional support tiers; custom pricing for enterprise contracts.

Enterprise pricing guardrails (talking points for AEs and SEs):
- Estimate approach: baseline = expected peak concurrent qps * average tokens per request * model token cost (from model catalog) adjusted for expected batching and caching savings (default 30% reduction assumption).
- Offerings to propose for pilots: 8–12 week PoC on Hosted with a performance plan, or 4–6 week Dedicated pilot (trial reserved capacity) for realistic latency and throughput validation.
- Discounting guidance: up to 20% on Hosted annual commitments; Dedicated discounts scale with multi-month/annual committed spend and size of reserved pool. Escalate >30% discounts to VP Sales.
- Commercial terms: Typical enterprise deals include a 12-month commitment, SLA clauses for uptime (99.9% for Dedicated), change control for model upgrades, and data residency clauses.

Example pricing worksheet (use during discovery) — plain text table for quick copy/paste:
MODEL_CLASS | EST_P95_LATENCY | RAW_TOKEN_COST/1k | EXPECTED_CACHE+BATCH_SAVINGS | EST_EFFECTIVE_COST/1k
- small-llm | 80ms | $0.25 | 30% | $0.175
- medium-llm | 180ms | $1.10 | 35% | $0.715
- large-llm | 380ms | $4.00 | 40% | $2.40

Commercial playbook steps for AEs: 1) Run discovery to capture expected qps/tokens and security requirements; 2) Use pricing worksheet to produce a 3-month forecast; 3) Propose pilot plan (Hosted/Dedicated); 4) If security/regulatory constraints exist, propose Private and route to Enterprise Sales engineer for scoping.

Approval gates: All non-standard discounts and T&Cs involving >4 week implementation timelines require RevOps and Legal approval.

Note: Always attach a TCO appendix showing assumptions for batching/caching savings and model selection to avoid sticker shock.
case_studies:
Customer A — FinTech analytics platform (Enterprise Private deployment)

- Solution: Private deployment behind customer VPC with KMS integration; preconfigured Dedicated pools for peak trading hours.
- Outcome: Achieved p95 <200ms for medium-LLM workflows, decreased inference ops burden by 70%, and reduced per-token cost by 28% after applying caching and quantization profiles.

- Solution: Migrated from Hosted API to Dedicated reserved pool; enabled intelligent routing and model variant fallbacks.
- Outcome: Stable p95 at 150ms, 35% reduction in average token cost, and 99.95% availability SLA met for peak periods.

security_faq:
Purpose: Provide concise, prospect-facing answers to common security questions during sales cycles. Refer complex requests to Security & Compliance.

Q: Where is customer data stored when using Redwood Hosted API?
A: All customer request and response metadata is stored in our encrypted storage with regional options; persisted data residency options are available for enterprise contracts and Private deployments.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A: Yes. We support KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments; HSM-backed key management is available for Private with an implementation plan.

Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC/on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control planes and a packaged on-prem deployment option. Implementation timelines typically range from 6–12 weeks depending on environment and compliance needs.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities do you provide?
A: Audit logging for admin events, model version changes, and user access is standard on Dedicated and Private. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs and retained per contractual retention policies.

Q: Do you perform third-party security assessments?
A: Redwood conducts annual third-party penetration tests and maintains SOC2 Type II [status as of 2026-06]. For specific audits, we can provide evidence under an NDA.

Q: How is access controlled?
A: RBAC with SSO integrations (OIDC/SAML) is available across our control plane. Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured to use customer IdP and attribute-based access controls.

Escalation: For prospect requests that require architecture diagrams, threat-model reviews, or specific compliance evidence, route to security@redwood.example.com and attach the prospect NDA template.

Speaker note: Keep security answers high level in discovery; move the prospect to a security review call within the first 2–3 weeks of a pilot when possible.

1) AE: Complete detailed discovery and fill pricing worksheet (owner: assigned AE).
2) SE: Run a focused benchmark (3–5 representative queries) on Hosted or Dedicated trial; capture p50/p95 and token counts (owner: assigned SE).
3) Solutions Architect: If Private required, scope network/KMS/ops requirements and produce SOW (owner: Solutions Architecture).
4) Security: Provide security pack and schedule security review if requested (owner: Security & Compliance team).
5) Legal/RevOps: Engage for non-standard discounts and contract review (owner: RevOps).
